summary: CitrineHealth live inference: fanout-induced head-of-line blocking causing high tail latency and streaming reassembly failures
description: CitrineHealth reported large increases in 95th/99th percentile request latency for live streaming completions during morning peak (08:30–09:20 UTC) followed by client-observed partial transcripts and session resumption failures. Initial triage showed many concurrent gRPC streams from the customer's application were being fanout-scheduled onto a small set of GPU workers, creating head-of-line blocking and delayed reassembly of chunked streaming frames. This ticket captures the incident timeline, investigation, mitigations, and post-incident follow-up with the customer.
impact: Customer-facing recommendation engine returned incomplete streaming responses for ~18% of requests during the incident window; sessions failing to resume resulted in manual retries from the client's end, increasing token usage and causing billing exposure. Business impact: degraded UX for CitrineHealth's triage app during morning peak; potential SLA exposure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open a high-concurrency streaming session to the Redwood API using gRPC or websocket streaming client.
2) Send interleaved short-prefix prompts across >200 concurrent streams pinned to the same session affinity key.
3) Observe tail latency spikes on the client and truncated final chunks when traffic concentrates on a reduced GPU worker set.
4) Reproduce more reliably when kernel-selection rollback (PR 2207) was applied to a subset of quantized nodes (see related PRs).
investigation_notes: 08:35 - Support received first alert from CitrineHealth via #support-escalations: high latencies and partial transcripts.
08:40 - On-call SRE (Diego) pulled p95/p99 token latency dashboards and tracing; spike correlated to a small subset of serving-runtime pods with increased queue depth.

08:55 - Observed that scheduler's fanout policy had grouped many small-stream requests into the same GPU worker due to an interaction between recent prefix-aware batching changes and session-affinity hash window.
09:10 - Tracing showed reassembly timeouts: chunk reassembly component retried and eventually dropped final chunks when interleaving exceeded expectation.
09:20 - CS escalated to Engineering; momentary autoscaler hiccup left a reduced worker pool size in us-east while request rates were higher than predicted.

09:35 - Hypothesis: combination of (a) scheduler affinity regression, (b) autoscaler underprovisioning during a deployment window, and (c) reassembly backpressure threshold too low for dense fanout patterns.
09:50 - Captured pcap-like stream logs and chunk sequence gaps; linked logs attached for postmortem.
10:10 - Emergency mitigation applied: tightened fanout circuit-breaker to limit per-worker concurrent streaming sessions and enabled conservative prefix windowing for session hashing.

resolution_summary: Applied emergency fanout circuit-breaker limiting per-worker streaming concurrency, temporarily increased worker pool in us-east, and disabled the aggressive prefix-aware batching change rolled earlier that morning. These mitigations restored normal tail latency and eliminated chunk reassembly timeouts. Customer confirmed improved behavior and we scheduled a formal rollback/patch pair for the scheduler and autoscaler interactions.
root_cause: A deployment earlier in the morning introduced a change to prefix-aware batching that altered session-affinity hashing. During morning traffic spike, the scheduler's new grouping pattern concentrated many small streaming sessions onto a reduced GPU pool (partially due to an autoscaler delay), creating head-of-line blocking and triggering chunk reassembly timeouts when chunk interleaving exceeded backpressure thresholds.
postincident_actions: 1) Engineering to implement a durable fix for session-affinity hashing to avoid pathological grouping (PR 2213 merged).
2) Autoscaler: add fallback fast-path to bypass quota-check stalls during active maintenance windows (INT-40321).
3) Update streaming reassembly component to tolerate higher interleaving and emit more actionable metrics (latency per-chunk-seq).
4) Runbook: create dedicated checklist for morning peak scale events and preflight verifications for kernel-selection rollouts.
5) Schedule a joint tech review with CitrineHealth on 2026-03-18; provide isolated test harness to reproduce load patterns.
6) Issue customer goodwill credit: 10% of March invoice applied as service credit (see billing note).
credits_or_billing_fix: Applied a 10% service credit to CitrineHealth's March invoice and opened finance ticket FIN-1298 to reconcile any downstream billing mismatches.
notes_for_postmortem: Action owner assignments and PR links included; need to collect additional chunk-level telemetry for next 14 days to confirm no recurrence. Recommend gating kernel-selection changes behind a stricter canary (region + low-concurrency synthetic test) before wide rollout.
